findings.finding: At tau=0.95 F-SIBS consumes MORE energy per image than centralized raw upload under all three radio profiles (1.45x WiFi, 1.51x BLE, 1.45x LoRa); median battery-lifetime extension factor 0.7x.
findings.evidence: E9_DF + E9_LIFE_DF recorded tables (measured uplink of the recorded federation run)
findings.interpretation: Unfavorable result preserved: the tau=0.95 uplink dominates the energy budget exactly as it dominates the bit budget in E04.
findings.limitation: Single measured run; order-of-magnitude radio constants; one scene.

findings.finding: The energy cost is radio-dominated: E_cpu = 0.001 mJ (negligible), E_rx is 1-4% of E_total; E_tx (uplink) carries >95% of F-SIBS energy.
findings.interpretation: Energy optimisation == uplink-bit optimisation; the levers are tau (E06) and group homogeneity (E05), not compute.
findings.limitation: CPU model is proportional-work only (same constant across schemes).

findings.finding: Local-SIBS uses zero radio energy (0.0010 mJ/image CPU-only) but delivers the lowest SSIM (0.7068 vs 0.7214 federated, 1.0 raw upload).
findings.interpretation: The energy-quality plane has a genuine three-way trade-off; the recorded tau=0.95 point is dominated by raw upload on BOTH axes, which is the honest headline.
findings.limitation: SSIM from one run; raw upload assumed lossless.

validation.detail: E_total == E_tx + E_rx + E_cpu for all rows: True
F-SIBS/raw energy ratio = 1.45x on WiFi at tau=0.95 (UNFAVORABLE, >1) -- preserved as a genuine finding; consistent with E04 uplink analysis and addressable via low-tau operation (E06)
SSIM constant per scheme across profiles: True
median lifetime extension factor = 0.7x (<1 means F-SIBS lifetime is SHORTER than raw upload at tau=0.95 -- preserved)

requires_confirmation.issue: At tau=0.95 the measured uplink makes F-SIBS costlier in energy than raw upload (extension factor 0.7x).
